summary.intent: Human-piloted mechanical ornithopter translating the photographed notebook principles into a reduced educational flight model and recognisable machine.
explicit_engineering_completions: 55 kg pilot and revised 173.9 kg dry mass budget
16 kW engine, 85% transmission and reflected drive inertia
Passive pitch damping, tail sizing and control coefficients

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Mute swan planform proportions, broad inner wing, rounded/tapered outer hand wing, aspect-ratio paragraph and wrist-span fraction.
unreadable_or_rejected: The 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is inconsistent with the other scaling and was excluded.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: The aircraft uses span_m=14 and wing_area_m2=14^2/8.29 ≈ 23.64 m^2.

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Curved-plate section context only; not used as a recovered full-scale coefficient table.
unreadable_or_uncertain: The multi-axis graph is ambiguous in the photograph and appears to be low-Re context.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: Supplied engineering inner/outer CL/CD anchor tables were used instead of inventing exact coefficients from the image.

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Ideal trajectory / required-force method and explicit human-carrying powered-ornithopter intent.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: The simulator computes actual aerodynamic forces from the moving wing geometry rather than prescribing the target trajectory.

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Straight-and-level flapping is cyclic rather than perfectly steady; lift and thrust vary through the cycle.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: No altitude-hold or force-prescription is added; powered flight remains genuinely unsteady.

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Longer low-speed working stroke, equal timing toward cruise, and wing-body resonant mass-spring interpretation.
unreadable_or_uncertain: Some marginal pencil revisions are not fully legible.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: Implemented theta = phi - b*sin(phi) with low-speed timing_bias=0.3 and cruise bias 0, while retaining spring/inertia driven phase dynamics.

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Local force direction from actual wing motion, fore/aft movement, overlap/closing on recovery, spring–inertia exchange and body-pitch reaction.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: Forces are resolved from each strip's instantaneous body-relative velocity after removing spanwise flow; sweep and mass coupling use the same wingPose geometry.

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Incidence, camber and thickness are distinct concepts; the later goshawk figure is an example of sectional variation rather than a swan blueprint.
unreadable_or_uncertain: The goshawk camber percentages are not treated as swan dimensions.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: Camber, twist and thickness are kept separate in the model; outer sections are thin and more cambered than the inner arm wing.

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Inner arm wing about 5–6% thick, outer hand wing thin curved/slotted plate, changing effective action in working and recovery strokes, and use of conventional tail/rudder controls.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: Inner thickness fraction 0.055, outer thickness fraction 0.008, overlapping recovery leaves, horizontal tail, fin/rudder and three-wheel landing gear are used as mechanical completions.

photo_interpretations.principle_used: Power as D*V in glide plus additional aerodynamic, trajectory and wing-inertia terms; springs redistribute energy but do not create net propulsion energy.
photo_interpretations.engineering_completion: The simulation tracks shaft work, aerodynamic dissipation, transmission/damping heat and control work separately; spring energy only enters through the coupled mechanics.

visual_design_choices.silhouette: Long light fuselage, high flapping shoulder crank, broad inboard wing and rounded tapered outer leaves derived from the swan study.
mechanical_features: Exposed crank mast and transmission cluster
Trussed tail boom with conventional tailplane and rudder
Three-wheel undercarriage with wheels rotating about the aircraft lateral axis
Seated pilot, seat, tank and engine package

limitations: The photographs do not specify a validated human-carrying structure, engine installation or aerodynamic coefficient set.
Missing appendices and unreadable marginal notes leave genuine gaps filled by supplied engineering assumptions.
The flight model omits unsteady wake effects, sectional pitching moments, flexible structure and overlap-flow interference.
